name: HTTP Header Checker
title: Header Checker: See Every HTTP Response Header
description: Free HTTP header checker: see every response header for a URL, with SEO-critical ones flagged — X-Robots-Tag, canonical Link, cache-control, HSTS.
answer: An HTTP header checker shows every response header a URL returns, including the first response if it redirects. SEO-critical headers are pulled out and explained: X-Robots-Tag, Link (canonical), Content-Type, Cache-Control, compression and HSTS. Enter a URL to see them.
trust: We request the URL live and show the raw headers exactly as your server or CDN returned them.
body:
## HTTP Header Checker: X-Robots-Tag, Cache and Redirects

Most headers don't matter for SEO; a few matter a lot because they can override what your HTML says.

| Header | Why it matters |
|---|---|
| X-Robots-Tag | Can noindex a page (or a PDF) without any meta tag |
| Link | Can declare rel=canonical or hreflang, mainly for non-HTML files |
| Location | The redirect target on 3xx responses |
| Content-Type | Pages must be text/html to be parsed as HTML |
| Cache-Control / ETag | Repeat-visit speed and efficient recrawling |
| Content-Encoding | gzip or brotli compression |
| Strict-Transport-Security | Forces HTTPS on future visits |

Google documents [X-Robots-Tag](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/robots-meta-tag) as equivalent to the robots meta tag — and it's the only option for files without HTML.

## HTTP Headers Check: What Each Header Does to SEO

The dangerous one is X-Robots-Tag, because it's invisible in the page source. A `noindex` header left over from staging removes pages from Google while the HTML looks perfectly fine.

It's rare on homepages — 2.9% of the 315 homepages we analyzed in October 2026 sent an X-Robots-Tag ([dataset](/resources/technical-seo-baseline-2026-10.json)) — but much more common on PDFs, feeds and environments copied from staging.

## Is my site compressing pages?

Check `Content-Encoding`. In our sample, 59% of homepages were served with brotli, 37.1% with gzip and 3.8% uncompressed. Uncompressed HTML is a free speed win waiting to happen: turning on gzip or brotli is usually a single server or CDN setting.

## How do I read the result?

Start with the status line, then the flagged SEO headers, then the full list. If the URL redirects, we also show the first response, because headers on a redirect (like a stray noindex) can matter too.

For definitions of any header you don't recognize, [MDN's header reference](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Headers) is the standard. To check the security headers specifically and get a grade, use the [security headers checker](/tools/security-headers-checker); for indexing directives in both tags and headers together, use the [meta robots checker](/tools/meta-robots-checker).

faqs.q: How do I check the HTTP headers of a website?
faqs.a: Enter the URL above. You can also use your browser's developer tools (Network tab) or run curl -I with the URL in a terminal to see the response headers.

faqs.q: Can an HTTP header noindex my page?
faqs.a: Yes. An X-Robots-Tag: noindex header tells Google not to index the URL, exactly like a robots meta tag, and it works on PDFs and images that can't carry meta tags.

faqs.q: Why do headers differ between this tool and my browser?
faqs.a: CDNs can vary responses by location, device, cookies or user agent, and browsers add cached responses. We show what a fresh request from our server receives.
